newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate dives 630 bps at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate dives 630 bps at close.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates ended down a substantial 630 basis points at 17.20 percent on Thursday.

Dealers said rates had eased down from a late speculative spike on Wednesday and accelerated their fall as investors bought paper in the wake of mild inflation data and strong trade figures, dealers said.
"Rates went up to ridiculously high levels on Wednesday, it was sheer speculation. One big player managed to jack rates up," a fixed-income analyst said.
Dealers said many banks were caught short on liquidity on Wednesday, which saw the cutoff date for settling balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank.
Big players took advantage of this situation, they added, to hold on to liquidity until the closing minutes to force smaller banks to pay high rates.
Dealers said stronger trade figures released early in the session added to market confidence that had emerged after relatively clean mid-term elections held on Sunday.

The Finance Ministry revised May trade figures up to a surplus of $220 million, from a preliminary $88 million. Dealers said this indicated the peso was strong enough to withstand a downward trend in interest rates.
Other dealers said secondary rates also fell in response to Tuesday's cuts in primary rates, a reaction that was delayed by Wednesday's liquidity squeeze.
Banco de Mexico drained 360 million pesos from the market through one overnight repo, which it assigned at 17.85 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile fell 240 basis points to 18.60 percent.
Liquidity of 973 million pesos was due to return to the system on Friday from prior central bank participation.
